PLAYGROUND LESSON · PLAYGROUND · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Sit — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches sitting down as a real skill: criss-cross legs, hands resting, body calm — the superpower that runs story time, circle time and every classroom after.

What is this?

Sit is coming to rest on the ground or a seat: cross the legs (criss-cross!), rest the hands, settle the body — sitting still is listening with your whole posture.

What does it mean?

Between the running and the climbing sits the sit — the skill that lets a child JOIN story time, assembly and every group moment. Framed as a skill (not a command), sitting calm becomes something children can practise and own.

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three sit ideas: criss-cross legs make a steady base — a basket the body sits in; hands REST — in the lap, on the knees, holding a book; and calm is the game — still body, soft face, ears open.

Why this matters

Group sitting is the gateway to every classroom skill for the next twelve years — taught here as a game on the grass, where it first belongs.

What it teaches

Postural control, stillness stamina (built in seconds, not demands), group calm, and the transition skill — running to sitting to running.

Words to learn

sitcriss-crosscalmstilllapstory timesettle

Say this to your child

“"Sitting down is a real skill! Cross your legs — criss-cross — and sit in the basket: steady base, tall back. Hands REST in your lap. Then the settle: three slow breaths, shoulders down — calm as a pond. Sitting calm lets you join every story, every circle, every song. Criss-cross… settle… listen!"”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "This is sit — the calm-down skill!"
  2. The basket: cross the legs — criss-cross — and sit INSIDE the basket: steady base, tall back.
  3. The resting hands: hands go to the lap or the knees — resting, not fidgeting. Try both; pick a home for the hands.
  4. The settle: three slow breaths, shoulders down, soft face — sitting calm is a game you can win.
  5. Play the sitting games below and close: "criss-cross, hands rest, settle."

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "Sit" stands in big navy capitals inside the rounded frame, with a friendly sitting illustration below — exactly as the criss-cross calm looks.

Ask your child

"What does criss-cross make — a basket or a puddle? Where do the hands rest? How many breaths in the settle?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "Criss-cross basket!" "Hands rest in my lap!" or the settled one: "Three breaths — calm as a pond!"

Out in the real world

Sitting moments fill every day: story time, meal time, bus seats, the cinema — and the criss-cross basket transfers to all of them. The settle is also the bedtime trick.

Try it together

Circle-Time Practice: everyone sits criss-cross in a circle — the settle, three breaths. Then story time for ONE minute (a very short story!) with statue-calm: still body, hands resting. Break, run a lap, sit again — the run-to-sit transition is the real skill. Three rounds, story a little longer each time. Criss-cross, hands rest, settle: the classroom superpower, grown on grass.

Understanding check

Ask: "What does criss-cross make? Where do the hands go? What is the settle?" A basket, the lap, three breaths — three answers and the circle is calm.

Parent tips

Seconds matter: ten calm seconds is a win at two, a minute is a triumph at four — grow slowly. And let the run-lap between sits be joyous: the transition is half the skill.

This lesson pairs with the Sit flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Playground.
